title: stats.comparison.holm_adjust
---



```python
stats.comparison.holm_adjust(p_values)
```

Adjust p-values for multiple testing with the Holm step-down method.

Sorts the raw p-values ascending (stable sort), multiplies the
``i``-th smallest by ``m - i`` remaining hypotheses, enforces
monotonicity with a running maximum, and caps at 1.0.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name     | Type                                     | Description                                                         | Default    |
|----------|------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| p_values | [pd](`pandas`).[Series](`pandas.Series`) | Raw p-values; the index identifies the hypotheses and is preserved. | _required_ |

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                     | Description                                               |
|--------|------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
|        | [pd](`pandas`).[Series](`pandas.Series`) | pd.Series: Adjusted p-values in the original index order. |

## Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises}

| Name   | Type                       | Description                                 |
|--------|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
|        | [ValueError](`ValueError`) | When ``p_values`` is empty or contains NaN. |

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}


::: {#2ef45dbb .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import pandas as pd
from spotforecast2_safe.stats.comparison import holm_adjust

raw = pd.Series([0.01, 0.02, 0.03, 0.04], index=list("abcd"))
adjusted = holm_adjust(raw)
print(adjusted.to_string())
assert list(adjusted) == [0.04, 0.06, 0.06, 0.06]
```
